name: Bug Fix
description: For fixing a bug: find and agree on the root cause first (RCA, which may install dependencies and run tests to reproduce the bug, reviewed up to 3 rounds), then fix it with tests (reviewed against the RCA, up to 3 rounds), get a human sign-off, then document and retro before the built-in Complete stage commits, pushes and raises the PR. Branches are always bugfix/….

steps.instructions:
Do a detailed root cause analysis (RCA) of the bug this task describes. Do not change any project files: this step is analysis only. You may run commands: install the project's dependencies and run its test suite (the registered testing tools, or the project's own test command). Installs and test runs are not committed, and you must not use commands to edit source files.

1. Reproduce the bug, or, when it can't be reproduced here, trace it through the code from the reported symptom. Install dependencies if needed and run the tests to reproduce the bug and to establish which tests fail before the fix. Say which you did and how (commands run, inputs used, code path followed), and record each command you ran and its result in the report's "Reproduction" and "Tests" sections. If dependencies can't be installed (no network, registry down), say so in the report.
2. Identify the root cause: the actual defect, not the symptom. Back it with evidence from the code: file paths with line numbers, the relevant snippets, and why they produce the reported behavior.
3. List the affected areas: every module, caller, data path or user-facing behavior the defect or its fix touches.
4. Propose a fix approach that removes the root cause, and name the tests that should prove it. Prefer a regression test that fails before the fix and passes after it, plus any further cases the affected areas need. For each test or check you propose, say who can run it: the Fix step (automated, from a shell) or a person at sign-off (hands-on, for example in a real browser or device). Never make a check the Fix step cannot perform a requirement of that step; list it as a sign-off check with the exact actions and expected results.

Call complete_step with a short summary and your full report as one output named "RCA report" (format "markdown") with the sections: Reproduction, Root cause, Evidence, Affected areas, Proposed fix, Tests. The Fix step works from this report and the reviewers check the fix against it, so it must stand on its own.

On a later round (after RCA Review found issues), address every point from the latest review and call complete_step again with the complete, updated RCA report as the output — not just the changes.
steps.name: RCA
RCA Review

steps.instructions:
Fix the bug according to the RCA step's latest "RCA report" (in Earlier stages' outputs), which RCA Review approved. Fix the root cause it identifies, not just the symptom, and cover the affected areas it lists. If you find the report is wrong somewhere, make the best fix you can and say clearly in your summary where and why you departed from it.

Write tests where they apply, following the report's proposed tests. The ideal is a regression test that fails before the fix and passes after it: where you can, confirm it fails without your fix. If no test applies, say why in your summary.

Your summary must say what you changed, which tests you added or changed, and what you ran to verify the fix.

On a later round (after Bugfix Review found issues, or after the human reviewer requested changes), fix every point from the latest review or request before calling complete_step again. Add your changes on top of the existing work.
steps.name: Fix
Bugfix Review

steps.instructions: Change documentation only: never source code or tests. Run a documentation-and-retro pass over this task's changes using the maintain-project-context skill. Store retro learnings in files (within the project or in the agent/skill file that executed this task), never in memory. Then handle every entry under "Planning gaps raised this run" in your prompt, if there is one: for each gap, reason about its root cause (why planning missed it, and what rule would have caught it). When the fix belongs to this project's own planning (a house rule the next planning session on this project should already know), write it into .docs/planning-notes.md right away (create it if missing; keep it a short, current list of rules grouped by topic, not a log of tasks), with no approval needed, the same as .docs/blueprint.md. Future planning sessions on this project read that file before they start. When the fix instead belongs in a shared Catalog Workflow step's instructions or in a Skill (used by every project, not just this one), do not apply it on your own: describe the exact proposed change and why it would have prevented the gap, ask the person directly in this session whether to apply it, and wait for their answer. Only after an explicit "yes" call update_workflow_step (workflow id, step id, the step's complete new instructions) or update_skill (skill id, the complete new SKILL.md body). On a "no", silence or an unclear reply, leave the shared definition unchanged and note the declined proposal in your summary. Your summary must list the docs you updated, the retro updates you made, and what you did about each planning gap.
steps.name: Docs & Retro
